slides.title: The Roadmap for Deliberate Evidence
bullets: Translates priority research questions into a coordinated set of studies
Often built directly from identified evidence gaps
Sets objectives, timelines, and owners for each activity
Ensures evidence generation follows strategy, not isolated initiatives

slides.title: Four Activity Types, One Plan
bullets: Phase IIIb and IV studies covering new populations and comparators
Investigator-initiated studies answering external scientific questions
Real-world data collection and disease registry collaborations
HEOR studies supporting access and reimbursement decisions

slides.title: Coherence Over Quantity
bullets: A good plan isn't judged by how many studies it contains
Every activity must answer a concrete strategic question
The set must balance science, market access, and clinical practice needs

slides.title: Four Construction Stages
bullets: Identify and prioritize evidence gaps, with direct MSL field input
Define specific, measurable evidence objectives with a clear timeline
Design the right study type for each objective
Allocate resources, timeline, and scientific review governance

slides.title: Where the MSL Plugs In
bullets: Gap identification: brings the systematized voice of the field
Execution and dissemination: supports investigator relationships
Helps published results reach the right scientific audience
Always through non-promotional scientific communication

slides.title: A Cycle That Outlives Launch
bullets: Each study answering a real gap generates new evidence
New evidence often reveals new questions
That continuous cycle keeps the product scientifically relevant
Credibility extends well beyond the initial approval moment

takeaway.title: The evidence generation plan turns prioritized gaps into a coherent, resourced roadmap of studies across a product's life
bullets: MSL field insight shapes both gap prioritization and execution support
Coherence across study types matters more than sheer study count
Each study answered fuels the next question in a continuous cycle
